translationRepairs: Penalties must strike the balance—no empty preaching—and so the Five Thearchs knew exile and execution, while the Three Dynasties relied on capital punishment and branding.
Penalties must strike the balance—no empty preaching—and so the Five Thearchs knew exile and execution, while the Three Kings relied on capital punishment and branding.
s0020 三王 means the Three Kings; 'Three Dynasties' invents a dynasty reading the Chinese does not support.
Your Majesty restored order with virtue surpassing Kings Wen and Wu—you must not cling to the dying expedients of the late Han.

Your Majesty embraces primal virtue and has acted as the times required to restore order; your achievements surpass those of Kings Wen and Wu, and your virtue matches that of the Exalted Emperor. You truly should not follow the declining precedents of the dynasty's final years.

In this conventional pairing, 文、武 are the Zhou Kings Wen and Wu, while 高皇 refers separately to Han Gaozu. The revision restores the omitted Gaozu comparison without changing the Zhou kings into Han emperors.
During Yongchu Liang Hu served as prefect of Changle. Liang Song the elder's younger brother—also named Liang Song but styled Shujing—is introduced next.
During Yongchu he served as prefect of Changle. Song's younger brother was Song.
s0065 only records the Yongchu Changle shaofu appointment and 松弟竦; the original invents Shujing and forward narrative from the next unit.
Emperor Xiaozong afterward edict heard return native commandery.
Emperor Xianzong afterward by edict permitted return to the native commandery.
顯宗 romanizes as Xianzong; Xiaozong would require 孝宗, which the Chinese does not have.
Grand Commandant Zhang Pu questioned Liang Shan on the facts; when the empress received Shan, Zhang explained the memorial.
Grand Commandant Zhang Pu questioned Liang Shan on the merits; shortly afterward Shan was summoned to audience, and Zhang then explained Shan's memorial.
會後召見 names no empress host; the following unit's 帝 shows the audience was imperial, so inventing an empress is unsupported.
Fan Diao came from a collateral line of Fan Hong, who had served as superintendent of the imperial household.
Diao was the great-grandson of the elder brother of Fan Hong, the superintendent of the imperial household.
光祿大夫宏兄曾孫 makes Diao the great-grandson of Hong's elder brother, not a collateral descendant of Hong himself.
The edict continues: I will not launch novel ceremonies lightly; past emperors left clear models for ennobling a sovereign's maternal kin.
I dare not lightly undertake new rites; reviewing former ages, Taizong and Zhongzong truly had old canons of posthumously charging the maternal grandfather to deepen kinship.
The original drops the named models 太宗、中宗 and the specific act 追命外祖; the proposal restores both.
He had kite shoulders, jackal eyes, sunken glaring sidelong gaze, and a stammer—barely able to read and reckon.
冀字伯卓 only states the courtesy name; the physiognomy belongs to s0149 為人鳶肩豺目….
He had kite shoulders, jackal eyes, sunken gleaming eyes gazing sidelong, stammered tongue—barely literate.
The literal of the same unit likewise copies s0149's description onto 冀字伯卓; only the courtesy name belongs here.
Yangjia 1 made his daughter empress; Shang gained rank, land, a ceremonial carriage, and Bearer of the Golden Mace.
Yangjia 1 made his daughter empress and his younger sister an honored lady; Shang gained rank, land, a ceremonial carriage, and Bearer of the Golden Mace.
陽嘉元年…妹為貴人 is present in the Chinese but omitted from the idiomatic English; the proposal restores it.
Yonghe 4: eunuchs accused Shang and Cao Teng of plotting succession.
Yonghe 4: Zhang Da, Qu Zheng, Shi Guang, Fu Fu, and Du Yong plotted to accuse Shang and palace attendants Cao Teng and Meng Ben of plotting succession.
The Chinese names the five conspirators and includes Meng Ben among the accused; collapsing them to 'eunuchs…Cao Teng' omits that content.
The court escorted; the emperor watched from Xuanyang.
The empress personally escorted; the emperor watched from Xuanyang pavilion.
中宮親送 means the empress (central palace) personally escorted; 'the court' invents a generic subject.
Before Shang was buried Shangdi named Ji Grand General and younger brother Buyi governor of Henan.
Before Shang was buried, Emperor Shun named Ji Grand General and younger brother Buyi governor of Henan.
順帝 is Emperor Shun; 'Shangdi' is a mistranslation unsupported by the graphs.

Sun Fen, a man of Fufeng, was wealthy but miserly by nature. Liang Ji used a team of horses to make him a gift and asked to borrow 50,000,000 cash. Fen gave him 30,000,000. Ji was furious and therefore reported to the commandery and county that Fen's mother had been his slave guarding storehouses and had stolen ten hu of white pearls and 1,000 jin of purple gold before absconding. He then arrested and interrogated Fen and his brothers, who died in prison, and confiscated all their property, more than 170,000,000 cash.

Shisun Fen, a man of Fufeng, was wealthy but miserly by nature. Liang Ji used a team of horses to make him a gift and asked to borrow 50,000,000 cash. Fen gave him 30,000,000. Ji was furious and therefore reported to the commandery and county that Fen's mother had been his slave guarding storehouses and had stolen ten hu of white pearls and 1,000 jin of purple gold before absconding. He then arrested and interrogated Fen and his brothers, who died in prison, and confiscated all their property, more than 170,000,000 cash.
士孫奮 is the compound surname Shisun plus given name Fen; rendering the surname as Sun invents a different family name.

Wealthy miser Shifu Fen of Fufeng—Ji lent horses demanding fifty million; Fen gave thirty—Ji accused Fen's mother as stolen slave girl with phantom gems—executed Fen brothers and seized seven hundred million assets.

Wealthy miser Shisun Fen of Fufeng—Ji lent horses demanding fifty million; Fen gave thirty—Ji accused Fen's mother as stolen slave girl with phantom gems—executed Fen brothers and seized over one hundred seventy million assets.
Literal 'Shifu' corrupts 士孫, and 億七千餘萬 is over 170 million, not seven hundred million.
Once every ten days one man would balance the Masters of Writing affairs.
Every ten days he would enter to oversee the affairs of the Masters of Writing.
In context of Liang Ji's privileges, 十日一人，平尚書事 means he enters every ten days to decide Shangshu affairs, not that an anonymous 'one man' balances them.
He built a vast Rabbit Park west of Luoyang.
He built a vast Rabbit Park west of Henan city.
This unit says 河南城西, not 洛陽; replacing Henan city with Luoyang invents a place-name the Chinese does not use here.
Deng Meng was Deng Xiang's daughter by Lady Xuan; after Xiang died Xuan married Liang Ji, who stood in an uncle's relation to Sun Shou.
Earlier, Deng Xiang of the harem and his wife Xuan bore a daughter Meng; when Xiang died, Xuan remarried a man named Liang Ji.
s0224 only has remarriage to 梁紀; Sun Shou, the uncle relation, and identity with Grand General 梁冀 are imported from later units or conflation.
That same Liang Ji was uncle to Sun Shou on her mother's side.
This Liang Ji was the maternal uncle of Ji's wife Sun Shou.
'That same Liang Ji' equates 梁紀 with 梁冀; the Chinese instead identifies 梁紀 as 冀妻壽之舅, a distinct person.
